title: justz command registry
description: The shape of commands.json, the registry justz reads for the rich variant. It checks types and nesting only: unknown fields are allowed, and whether the registry matches the justfile is the job of justz check.

$schema.description: The URL of this schema, so an editor can complete and check the file.

$comment.description: A note for readers. justz generate writes one as a header.

name.description: The heading of the help. Falls back to the directory name.

title.description: An alias justz reads when name is missing. Prefer name.

tagline.description: A one-line summary shown under the heading.

subtitle.description: An alias justz reads when tagline is missing. Prefer tagline.

cli.description: The command name shown in usage lines and examples, and the name of the shim.

groups.description: The command groups by key. The key core holds the top-level recipes; any other key is a module, run as just <group> <command>.

tiers.description: Ordered, headed sections of groups in the summary.

order.description: justz fmt sorts it, with core first. Nothing else reads it.

dispatchers.description: justz fmt sorts it A to Z. Nothing else reads it.

lab.description: justz fmt sorts it A to Z. Nothing else reads it.

groups.description: Keys of the groups in this section.

label.description: The human-readable name of the group.

extra.description: Documented entries that do not run as just <group> <command>.

desc.description: What the command does, imperative, with no trailing period.

detail.description: Longer prose about the command. Only the zoom (justz help <group> <command>) shows it. Keep desc to one line.

example.description: A usage example, prefixed with the ellipsis mark.

exits.description: Exit codes and what they mean, as {"0": "done"}. A key is an integer from 0 to 255; justz check reports any other key. The schema cannot express that, so it only says object of strings.

additionalProperties.description: What the exit code means, one line.

env.description: Environment variables the command reads, as rows. A flag goes in args, a variable here. justz check reports a row without a name, a duplicate name and a wrong type; it cannot tell whether the command reads the variable.

seeAlso.description: Keys of related commands, as group.command (core.build for a top-level command). justz check reports a key that does not exist.

name.description: The flag or positional name, such as -s, --surface <name>.

type.description: Real registries use boolean or string. justz does not read it.

values.description: The allowed values of an enum. They drive completion.

name.description: The variable name, such as STORAGE_HOST (upper case letters, digits and underscores).

required.description: True when the command fails or is wrong without the variable.

default.description: The value used when the variable is not set, as text. It is shown, not parsed.

cmd.description: The command line, written as just <group> <command> ...
